decisions.statement: A rule decides a category by naming the category.
A rule naming no category leaves a person to settle the transaction.
A rule gives the same answer every time the rule is run.
A rule's amounts accumulate as its price rises rather than being replaced.
A rule names a category by slug.
A category renamed in Monarch strands no rule.
A rule is data rather than code.
Nothing a rule states is executed.

definition: a written rule deciding what a transaction counts as

directives.name: The Failure Worth Having
directives.act: Prefer the clause that fails by matching nothing to the one that fails by matching wrongly.
directives.warrant: An unmatched row waits where somebody sees it; a wrong category becomes a total nobody checks.
aids: Never add a tolerance or widen a date window.
Never tighten a clause until it catches nothing.

directives.name: The Rows It Will Catch
directives.act: Weigh a rule by the rows it will catch rather than the rows it has caught.
directives.warrant: What a rule is worth is entirely ahead of it, and the rows behind are the only ones you can count.
aids: Ask Alan whether the charge will come again.
Write a subscription's rule on its first row.
